verdict: Vertex grew revenue 12% to $3.44B on cystic fibrosis strength and fast-growing newer medicines, but $502M of Crinetics acquisition costs cut GAAP profit to $654M.

segments.name: Cystic fibrosis products
segments.note: CF medicines: TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO $2,437M, ALYFTREK $706M and other CF products $131M — up 8% YoY.

segments.name: Other products
segments.note: CASGEVY (gene therapy) $99M, JOURNAVX (pain) $58M and PALSONIFY (from the Crinetics acquisition) $10M — small but growing fast.

opex.name: Research & development and acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research spending of $1,321M plus $41M of acquired in-process R&D. GAAP R&D includes $282M of Crinetics acquisition-related compensation.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company — includes $220M of Crinetics acquisition-related costs, and is net of a $4M gain from revaluing contingent consideration (reported combined figure $841M in whole $M).

otherDetail: Interest income $118M, less interest expense $36M and other expense $12M — $71M net in whole-$M figures (the release reports $70.5M).
oneTimers: About $502M of this quarter's GAAP expenses were Crinetics Pharmaceuticals acquisition-related costs — $282M in research & development and $220M in selling, general & administrative, mostly compensation for cash-settled Crinetics equity awards plus deal costs. Excluding these and other non-GAAP items, non-GAAP net income was $1,214M ($4.76 per share) versus GAAP net income of $654M ($2.56 per share), and non-GAAP operating income was $1,412M versus GAAP $713M.

takeaways.title: The base kept growing
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 12% to $3.44B. CF products grew 8% to $3.27B, led by ALYFTREK at $706M, and Vertex raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $13.15B–$13.25B.

takeaways.title: Diversification is showing up
takeaways.text: Non-CF products — CASGEVY $99M, JOURNAVX $58M and new PALSONIFY $10M — brought in $168M, more than four times a year ago, as Vertex adds endocrine and (soon) kidney franchises.

takeaways.title: Profit fell on deal costs
takeaways.text: GAAP net income dropped from $1,083M to $654M almost entirely because of $502M of Crinetics acquisition costs. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $9.8B after paying for the deal.
